critical_gaps: HARDWARE REALITY CONTRADICTS THE ENTIRE LLM PLAN. The llm-serving pillar's whole feasibility argument rests on 'a single 24GB consumer GPU (RTX 4090/3090)' running vLLM/SGLang. The actual box in C:\Agentic has Intel Iris Xe integrated graphics (NO discrete GPU, NO CUDA, effectively no usable VRAM for inference), a 12th-gen mobile CPU, and 15.7GB TOTAL system RAM. On this hardware the pillar's own numbers collapse: it explicitly states CPU-only llama.cpp does 'single-digits to low-tens of tokens/sec' and is 'viable only for a few hundred low-liveliness agents' - not 5000. The architecture doc MUST state the real target hardware. If the dev box IS the deployment box, 5000 LLM-lively agents is infeasible as scoped; if a 24GB+ NVIDIA box is assumed, that must be procured/specified and every tok/s number re-derived. Also note 15.7GB RAM must be shared by JVM heap + 5000 Player objects + region grid + OS + any local model - the co-location RAM budget was never computed and is likely the binding constraint before GPU even matters.

NO CODE IS ON DISK; NOTHING WAS LOCALLY VERIFIED OR BUILT. C:\Agentic contains only the L2 client and a research script - no Mobius clone, no Java, no build.xml, no Server.ini, no OfflinePlayTable.java. Every Mobius and protocol claim came from GitLab's unauthenticated REST tree + raw-file reads (the pillars admit GitLab web UI/search failed). Load-bearing internals were explicitly INFERRED not read: ScriptExecutor's runtime-compilation mechanism, FakePlayerHolder fields, FakePlayerInfo packet contents, and crucially the claim that the null-client write path tolerates 5000 ACTIVE (not idle) synthetic players. The architecture is built on unbuilt, unexecuted, partially-inferred code.

THE 5000-SCALE CLAIM HAS ZERO EMPIRICAL SUPPORT AND CONTRADICTS THE ONE HARD NUMBER FOUND. Mobius's own Server.ini sets MaximumOnlineUsers=2000 as the single-instance design ceiling for real Players - and design-B synthetic players ARE full Player objects carrying full per-Player cost. 5000 real-Player-equivalents is 2.5x the vendor's stated ceiling. OfflineTrader/OfflinePlay precedents are for tens-to-hundreds of IDLE/standing-still characters, not 5000 pathfinding, combat-taking, broadcasting agents. L2Solo's '~1,700 bots' is a runtime TARGET; its repo hardcodes only ~65 static bots and its LLM concurrency is deliberately capped at 32 concurrent / 240 req per 60s. No pillar presents a measurement of even 500 active synthetic players. The single biggest project risk - per-agent cost of movement+combat+broadcast+aggro-scan+pathfinding at scale - is unmeasured across ALL five pillars.

LLM REQUEST-RATE MATH IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT WITH THE TIERED-AI DESIGN. The llm-serving pillar computes 83-167 req/s by assuming ALL 5000 agents hit the LLM every 30-60s. The tiered-ai pillar contradicts this: it says the LLM is confined to Tier 2 (HOT agents only, budget-gated) at 'single-digit to low-double-digit calls/sec across the whole population' and 'most agents touch an LLM only every few minutes to hours.' These are off by ~10-50x. The two pillars never reconcile whether the LLM cadence is per-agent-every-60s (llm-serving's 83 req/s) or per-HOT-agent-only (tiered-ai's <=10 req/s). The token/cost math, GPU sizing, and feasibility verdict all depend on which is true, and the doc currently contains both.

THE 'ATTENTION WINDOW' ASSUMPTION IS UNVALIDATED AND MAY NOT HOLD FOR L3. Both llm-serving and tiered-ai make feasibility depend on LLM cost scaling with PLAYER attention, not agent count (only HOT/near-player agents think expensively). L2Solo's entire LOD model is SINGLE-real-player-centric and MUST be generalized to multi-center for L3 (l2solo pillar flags this as 'the main adaptation area'). But no pillar establishes L3's actual player-distribution assumption. If L3's premise is a believable LIVING WORLD (a near-empty server made to look populated) then real players may be very few - which HELPS. But if the design wants 5000 agents that are convincingly human to EACH OTHER and to bot-hunters across many regions simultaneously, the small-attention-window shortcut evaporates and cost explodes. This premise is the hinge of the whole cost model and is never pinned down.

LICENSING IS AN UNRESOLVED, POTENTIALLY PROJECT-KILLING CONFLICT. Mobius is mid-migration GPLv3->MIT; until complete, any distribution containing a single GPLv3 file is GPLv3 as a whole (copyleft). L3's synthetic-player subsystem is built directly ON Mobius (OfflinePlayTable/AutoPlayTaskManager derivation) = a derivative work = GPL. L2Solo is Apache-2.0 (permissive) but its code cannot be merged (different language) - only its design is reusable, which carries no license, so that's fine. The unresolved question: can L3 be closed-source/commercial at all? If yes, a per-file header audit of every reused Mobius file is mandatory BEFORE building, and GPL-only files need clean-room reimplementation. No pillar resolved whether L3 intends to distribute, sell, or keep private - which determines whether GPL even bites.

PROTOCOL/CLIENT MATCH IS UNVERIFIED AGAINST THE ACTUAL LOCAL CLIENT + GAMEGUARD WILL LIKELY BLOCK DEV SMOKE-TESTING. The '746' revision is not in any readable client file - it lives in the packed/GG-protected L2.exe and is only observable on the wire. So the SPECIFIC client build in C:\Agentic\Lineage2_Interlude_Client has NOT been confirmed to match Mobius CT_0_Interlude's 746 packet expectations. Worse, npkcrypt/GameGuard.des ARE present, and GameGuard will block or crash the real client unless the server does the expected GG exchange or the client is patched/GG-disabled. Milestone-1 (one real client logs in and SEES synthetic players) - the ONLY way to validate the whole approach visually - is gated on solving GameGuard, which no pillar has a concrete plan for.

SYNTHETIC-PLAYER SUBSYSTEM-INTEGRATION HAZARDS ARE IDENTIFIED BUT NOT DESIGNED. The protocol pillar lists NPE/persistence landmines: PlayerAutoSaveTaskManager must be disabled for synthetics; mail/clan/olympiad/siege/party subsystems assume a DB-backed char and live client and may NPE or persist garbage; every getClient() call needs null-guarding. These are flagged as risks but there is no design for how synthetic players participate in (or are gated out of) each subsystem - and 'gated out of clans/parties/economy' directly undercuts the 'human-like, socializing, grouping' goal from the tiered-ai pillar. There is a latent contradiction: the cheapest-to-integrate synthetic player is one gated out of most systems, but the most human-like one participates in all of them (and costs the most and risks the most NPEs).
feasibility_verdict: CONDITIONALLY FEASIBLE as a design, NOT feasible as currently scoped on the hardware actually present, and NOT YET PROVEN at 5k scale by any measurement. The architecture is coherent and the two synthetic-player hooks (Mobius OfflinePlay + null-client Player, driven by an L2Solo-style tiered/budgeted controller) are real and well-chosen. But 'up to ~5000 LLM-driven human-like players on a single box' overloads three independent unknowns that no pillar resolved: (1) HARDWARE - the box in C:\\Agentic is Intel Iris Xe integrated graphics + 15.7GB RAM, on which the LLM plan is impossible; the design silently assumes a 24GB NVIDIA GPU box that does not exist here and must be specified and budgeted. (2) SCALE - 5000 active Player objects is 2.5x Mobius's own 2000-user ceiling, and no test above ~65-1700 (mostly idle) bots exists anywhere in the evidence; the make-or-break number (per-active-agent CPU/memory/broadcast cost) is unmeasured. (3) LLM CADENCE - the req/s math is internally contradictory (83-167 req/s vs <=10 req/s) by 10-50x. The honest verdict: 5000 as a POPULATION with a small bounded LLM-ACTIVE subset (tens to low hundreds hot) is plausible IF a proper discrete GPU is provisioned AND the attention-window/few-real-players premise holds AND a staged load test (500->2000->5000) actually passes. 5000 SIMULTANEOUSLY LLM-thinking, fully-social, fully-simulated agents on one box is not supported by any evidence and likely infeasible. Proceed only after: pinning the real deployment hardware, running a scale load test to find the active-agent knee, reconciling the LLM cadence, and resolving GPL. Treat the current 5k figure as an aspirational ceiling, not a validated requirement.
contradictions: LLM request rate: llm-serving pillar computes 83-167 req/s (all 5000 agents think every 30-60s); tiered-ai pillar states 'single-digit to low-double-digit calls/sec' with most agents touching the LLM only every few minutes to hours - a 10-50x discrepancy that changes GPU sizing and the feasibility verdict.
Scale ceiling: Mobius Server.ini declares MaximumOnlineUsers=2000 as the single-instance design capacity, but the project targets 5000 full-Player-equivalent synthetics (2.5x) with no reconciliation.
Hardware assumption vs reality: llm-serving assumes a single 24GB NVIDIA GPU; the actual box is Intel Iris Xe integrated graphics + 15.7GB shared RAM - mutually exclusive.

Human-fidelity vs safe integration: the human-like/social goal wants synthetic players in parties, clans, and the economy, while the protocol pillar's low-NPE-risk advice is to gate them OUT of exactly those subsystems.

Reusability framing: the brief says L3 'incorporates L2Solo,' but L2Solo is C4/Node.js and CANNOT be code-merged into an Interlude/Java Mobius core; only its architecture (design, not code, no license transfer) is reusable - the brief overstates the integration.

Idle-vs-active precedent: OfflinePlay/OfflineTrader (tens-to-hundreds of idle chars) is used as proof of feasibility for 5000 actively-simulated agents, which is a different order of load the precedent does not establish.
must_answer_questions: What is the ACTUAL deployment hardware? Specifically: is there a discrete NVIDIA GPU with >=24GB VRAM, or is the target the Intel Iris Xe / 15.7GB box currently in C:\Agentic? This single answer determines whether the LLM plan is possible at all. If no discrete GPU, the doc must either specify procurement or redesign around a tiny CPU model serving only tens of hot agents.

What is the REAL LLM cadence and thus req/s ceiling - is the LLM called for every agent every ~60s (=~83 req/s, the llm-serving model) or only for a small HOT subset event-driven (=<=10 req/s, the tiered-ai model)? Reconcile the two pillars into ONE number and re-derive the GPU sizing and token budget from it.

What is the measured per-active-agent cost (CPU ms/tick, heap MB, broadcast fan-out, pathfinding) at 500 / 2000 / 5000 concurrently MOVING+FIGHTING synthetic Players on the target hardware, with one real client watching? Until this staged load test runs, the entire 5k premise is unvalidated - this is the make-or-break number and it does not exist yet.

How does L3 reconcile 5000 synthetic Players against Mobius's stated MaximumOnlineUsers=2000 single-instance ceiling? Raise it and prove it holds, shard, or reduce the fully-simulated count? What is the target ratio of fully-simulated (HOT/WARM) to statistically-fast-forwarded (COLD) agents at steady state?

What is L3's licensing intent - closed-source/commercial or open? Because L3 derives from GPLv3-era Mobius files, this determines whether a full per-file GPL-vs-MIT header audit + clean-room reimplementation of GPL-only pieces is mandatory before any code is written. Resolve GPL before committing engineering.

How is the ONE real developer/observer client's GameGuard handled - GG-disabled Mobius build, patched client, or GG auth emulation? Milestone-1 visual validation (a human sees synthetic players behaving plausibly) is impossible until this is answered, and no pillar has a concrete plan.

What is L3's real player-density premise? Few real players in a world made to LOOK alive (attention-window shortcut holds, cost is bounded) OR many players spread across many regions demanding many simultaneous HOT agents (shortcut fails, cost explodes)? The whole cost model hinges on this and it is never stated.

Which integration model for synthetic players - lightweight in-memory-synthesized (needs slim construction path + separate agent-state persistence, and must be gated out of DB-backed subsystems) or full DB-backed real character rows (full fidelity, survives restart, but full per-char cost x5000 and auto-save load)? And per subsystem (clan, party, olympiad, mail, siege, economy), do synthetics fully participate or are they gated out - given that gating them out undercuts the human-like/social goal?

Does the specific Interlude client build in C:\Agentic\Lineage2_Interlude_Client actually match Mobius CT_0_Interlude's 746 packet expectations? This requires a live login test and cannot be confirmed from files (746 is not stored in plaintext; it lives in the packed L2.exe).

How is the COLD->HOT reification/'popping' problem solved so statistically-fast-forwarded agents don't visibly teleport, jump levels, or show impossible inventory when a real player approaches? This is flagged as the top indistinguishability risk but has no concrete design, and it is the seam where the cheap-scale trick meets human observation.

What is the LLM per-hour/per-day TOKEN and DOLLAR budget, and target model? L2Solo defaults are tiny (320 max tokens, low reasoning); a genuinely human-like social quality bar likely needs a 7B+ model and larger outputs, which changes both the cost math and whether the chosen hardware can serve it.

What is ScriptExecutor's actual runtime-compilation mechanism (javax.tools JavaCompiler / ECJ / precompiled)? This decides JDK-vs-JRE deployment and whether behavior hot-reload is viable - and it was inferred, not read. Requires reading the actual file from a local clone.
